title: Introducing Claude Sonnet 5
description: Anthropic launched Claude Sonnet 5, its most agentic Sonnet model yet, capable of autonomous planning, tool use, and sustained multi-step work at a level that previously required larger models. It is now the default model for Free and Pro users worldwide, ships with a 1M-token context window, and launches with introductory pricing of $2/$10 per million input/output tokens through August 31, 2026.

title: The coding agent wars are spilling into the rest of the office: Claude Cowork
description: Anthropic expanded Claude Cowork, its agentic workspace assistant, to web and mobile by moving it fully to the cloud. Sessions and files now persist across devices, letting tasks keep running even after a user closes their laptop, extending Anthropic's coding-agent playbook into general office work.

title: Previewing GPT-5.6 Sol: a next-generation model
description: OpenAI opened a limited preview of its GPT-5.6 model family, led by the flagship Sol model alongside the Terra and Luna variants for everyday and low-cost use. Sol ships with OpenAI's most robust safety stack to date, adding strengthened protections against high-risk and cyber-related misuse, with pricing set at $5/$30 per million input/output tokens.

title: Introducing computer use in Gemini 3.5 Flash
description: Google made computer use a native built-in tool in Gemini 3.5 Flash, letting developers build agents that see, reason, and act across browser, mobile, and desktop environments. The capability was previously limited to a standalone Gemini 2.5 model and now ships with improved performance and enterprise safety guardrails via the Gemini API and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.

title: Nine and Microsoft announce Australian-first AI agreement for news media content
description: Australian media company Nine Entertainment and Microsoft announced a deal giving Nine's professional journalism a role in AI outputs generated for Microsoft Copilot users. It is described as a first-of-its-kind agreement between Microsoft and a major news publisher in Australia over how licensed content feeds AI-generated answers.

title: GitHub Copilot app available to all
description: GitHub rolled out the standalone GitHub Copilot app to all users, widening access beyond IDE integrations. The app packages Copilot's chat, agent, and coding-assistance features into a dedicated client for developers who want to work outside their editor.

title: Kimi K2.7 now available for Copilot Business and Enterprise
description: GitHub added Moonshot AI's Kimi K2.7 as a selectable model for Copilot Business and Enterprise customers, broadening the set of third-party models available inside Copilot's agentic coding workflows. The rollout follows GitHub's pattern of adding competing frontier and open models alongside its own in-house options.

title: CFOs and the new economics of AI
description: Cursor published an analysis of how finance leaders are budgeting for AI coding agents, arguing that per-seat software pricing models are giving way to usage-based spend tied to agent output. The piece draws on conversations with CFOs adapting cost controls and forecasting to agentic development tools.
